claims.text: The Z method can accurately calculate melting temperatures for high-melting refractory materials within a DFT framework.
The Z method can calculate entropy of fusion for high-melting refractory materials.
The Z method can calculate enthalpy of fusion for high-melting refractory materials.
The Z method can calculate volume change at the melting point for high-melting refractory materials.
The Z method requires only a fraction of the computational cost of full thermodynamic integration.
The Z method uses microcanonical, constant-energy ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
Homogeneous superheating in the proposed simulations generates solid-liquid coexistence.
The system should reach a metastable superheated state before melting occurs.
A transient two-phase solid-liquid state emerges during the superheating process.
Use of a microcanonical ensemble allows the Z method to bypass full thermodynamic integration.
Directly tracking energy changes associated with melting provides the melting temperature and latent heat.
Entropy and enthalpy of fusion can be derived from the latent heat obtained with the Z method.
The microcanonical energy changes directly provide the volume change at melting.
Z-method melting properties should closely agree with results from full thermodynamic integration.
The Z method should markedly reduce computational effort relative to full thermodynamic integration.
The reduced computational effort would make high-throughput screening feasible.
DFT-based free-energy calculations using extensive ab initio thermodynamic integration are accurate but computationally costly.
The efficacy of the method may be limited by the intrinsic accuracy of DFT and by complex free-energy landscapes in strongly anharmonic materials.
The Z method has been shown to reduce computational expense.
The accuracy of the Z method across refractory materials under extreme conditions still requires benchmarking against thermodynamic integration and experiments.
